scenario.title: Late shipments
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

F-01.statement: 300 orders are late at handover stage out of 1000 total orders

F-02.statement: Median pickup delay is 2.0 hours across 60 pickups.

F-03.statement: 21 out of 30 release batch runs failed; 290 orders released after pickup.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

CL-02.statement: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

H-REQ-FR-COMMS.statement: Customers lack real-time explanation for parcel delays, causing perceived lateness.

H-CARRIER-SCHED-DELAY.statement: Pickup schedule changes require carrier confirmation, leading to missed pickup windows and delays.

H-WAREHOUSE-PROC-DELAY.statement: Warehouse job processing bottlenecks increase order-to-dispatch time.

H-ORDER-DATA-ERROR.statement: Incorrect order data leads to misrouting or missed pickups.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows 300 late out of 1000 orders at the handover stage, indicating that handover accounts for 30% of lateness and points to handover delays as a contributing factor.
The observation shows a median pickup delay of 2 hours across 60 pickups, indicating that pickup operations contribute to overall shipment lateness.

E-03.content: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states that carrier pickup occurs two hours late, which explains the observed parcel lateness.

The observation shows that 21 of 30 release batch runs failed and 290 orders were released after pickup, indicating warehouse processing issues that can cause orders to miss pickup windows and contribute to lateness.

E-05.content: Carrier contract §3: pickup schedule changes run after SH-CAR confirms.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The carrier contract states that any pickup schedule change can only occur after SH-CAR confirms, indicating that schedule modifications require carrier approval.

U-U1.question: Can the carrier wait for delayed orders without impacting schedule?

U-U1.safe_placeholder: Assume carrier cannot wait; proceed with schedule adjustment.

U-U2.decision_impact: Potential trade‑off between release speed and packing quality.

U-U2.safe_placeholder: Assume optimizations do not harm downstream steps.

U-U3.decision_impact: If handover contributes less than observed, focusing on pickup may over‑correct.
U-U3.resolution_path: Collect lateness breakdown by stage for a representative sample period.
U-U3.safe_placeholder: Assume handover stage accounts for ~30% as observed.

trace.summary: An agent is needed to continuously monitor release performance and trigger corrective actions (e.g., schedule adjustments or process interventions) because structural changes alone do not guarantee ongoing compliance with pickup windows (U-U3).

structural_remedies.description: Optimize warehouse release timing by improving WMS job success rate and reducing failed release batch runs (E-04).
structural_remedies.rationale: No carrier approval required; relies on internal process change (K-SCHED not applicable).; residual gap: Some lateness may persist due to handover delays and other downstream factors (E-01 shows 30% of lateness at handover).

structural_remedies.description: Adjust carrier pickup schedule later to align with actual warehouse release times, requiring carrier confirmation (E-05).
structural_remedies.rationale: Carrier schedule change needs SH-CAR confirmation; domain authorization DA-PUSH-PICKUP-SCHEDULE granted to SH-CAR makes this feasible if confirmation obtained.; residual gap: Warehouse processing bottleneck remains; orders may still be released after the new schedule if delays worsen (E-04).

structural_remedies.description: Implement real-time monitoring of warehouse release timing with alerts for deviations (E-04, DA-WMS).
structural_remedies.rationale: Monitoring does not require external approvals; uses existing data assets.; residual gap: Root cause (warehouse bottleneck) is not eliminated; only visibility is improved (E-04).

proposal.summary: Problem: Warehouse processing bottlenecks cause orders to be released after the scheduled carrier pickup time, resulting in missed pickups and late shipments. [E-04][E-01]  Established by: The problem was established using evidence that 300 of 1,000 orders were late at the handover stage (E-01) and that 21 of 30 release batch runs failed, releasing 290 orders after pickup (E-04). Assumptions link handover lateness to missed pickup (A-A2) and suggest improving warehouse release timing reduces missed pickups (A-A3).  Released: The release includes optimizing warehouse release timing (WMS jobs) and adjusting the carrier pickup schedule (pickup-sched). [solution_design.release_scope]  Decision rationale: The gate resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs, leading to a RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION decision because the blocking scope (monitor_release_timing:DA-WMS) is outside the release scope and VOB-U-U3 remains open. [release.decision][release.limitations]  Known limitations: The release does not resolve the unknown proportion of lateness attributable to handover versus other stages (U-U3) and any schedule changes require carrier confirmation (K-SCHED, E-05). The handoff H-PICK delivery/semantic validity is also unknown. [U-U3][K-SCHED][E-05]
key_points: Problem defined as warehouse bottlenecks causing missed pickups.
Established via handover lateness (E-01) and failed release batches (E-04).
